summary.headline: GNFC Q2 FY27: management cited a ~INR 200 crore sequential operating profit drop; one-time net impact of ~INR 75 crore; cash and deposits ~INR 3,900 crore.
summary.overview: Management described a year-on-year improvement but a sequential margin squeeze in Q2 FY27, driven by realisation erosion in WNA, TGU and AN Melt, higher coal-linked fuel cost, and a wage settlement provision. Net one-time impacts were about INR 75 crore, which management said would have made the quarter INR 75 crore higher without them. H1 capex was about INR 500 crore, the captive coal-based steam plant is operational, and working capital rose on subsidy receivables. Management declined to comment on Q3 trends or current prices, citing price-sensitive information rules, so forward visibility was limited.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: Operating results improved, driven by volumes and energy norm gains. Urea concession accrual includes INR 61 crore positive impact from revised energy norm (6.20 to 6.37), booked in Q2 as subsidy.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Margins under pressure from realisation erosion in WNA, TGU, AN Melt and a fourth product, plus higher coal-linked fuel cost. Segment profit cited at INR 177 crore for Q2.

segments.name: TDI
segments.commentary: Q2 production was 8,700 tonnes, lower QoQ after July shutdown of about 30-35 days for cash-loss reasons. Indian capacity 70,000 tpa against a ~120 kt market; Wanhua commissioned a 360 kt plant.

segments.name: Ammonia, TGU, AN Melt, WNA, CNA (Q2 production)
segments.commentary: Ammonia ~1,78,000 t, TGU 44,900 t, AN Melt ~41,000 t, WNA 1,14,000 t, CNA 41,000 t. Acetic acid and ethyl acetate also restarted after July shutdown.

guidance_outlook: No quantitative guidance given. Management declined to comment on Q3 trends, October prices or current spreads, citing price-sensitive rules.
Captive coal-based plant: guaranteed test run for full-scale operation expected in Q3 FY27, after which it moves to full scale; steam benefit already realised, power still costlier than grid.
One project has a three-month delay; recovery plan agreed with lump-sum turnkey contractor. Others broadly on schedule.
Wage settlement accruals expected to continue in coming quarters; management said one-time items other than wage-related should not recur.
Nutrient-based subsidy rates for Rabi season not yet announced; NITI Aayog reviewing fixed cost of urea industry.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR 500 crore; ongoing projects broadly on schedule, with one project delayed by three months.
Captive coal-based plant generating steam since 25 July 2026 and supplying power since around August; power currently sourced mainly from grid as coal cost makes grid cheaper.
Four current projects listed in the investor presentation; management referred to the presentation for capital allocation plans.
TDI capacity 70,000 tpa at Bharuch and Dahej; no plan to shut Bharuch, which management said is now broadly cost-competitive with Dahej.
Plants restarted after July shutdown; Q2 volumes were below Q1 for TDI, acetic acid and ethyl acetate.
demand_pricing: Chemical pricing is import-parity based except for one or two products; Chinese capacity additions are driving competition, with Wanhua adding a 360 kt plant.
Realisation erosion in WNA, TGU, AN Melt and one other product drove the sequential margin decline; management said linkage to crude and gas has broken down.
Indian TDI market about 120 kt, growing at about 8-9% CAGR; all major foam manufacturers are customers.
Q2 average prices: TDI ~INR 285,000, aniline ~INR 238,000, acetic acid ~INR 72,840, WNA ~INR 28,500 (100% basis). Management said TDI last week of September was ~INR 310,000.
Gas availability was affected early in the war; feed availability otherwise not an issue. Procurement is based on monthly production plan, with no stock-up on price speculation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating profit fall ~INR 200 crore QoQ when spreads were steady or higher and oil input was lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited realisation hits in WNA, TGU, AN Melt and one more product, higher coal cost for fuel, and a wage settlement provision effective 1 July. Gas and oil prices were broadly unchanged QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the chemicals drop is one-time, and is Q3 likely to normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Net one-time impact was about INR 75 crore across the business, including INR 33 crore wage settlement; management said wage accruals will continue. Management declined to comment on Q3 trends.

qa_highlights.question: Has the INR 61 crore energy norm benefit been booked in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. It is booked as a concession rate revision on urea, recorded as subsidy receivable and subsidy income within fertilizer revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Chinese TDI capacity additions, customer concentration and Bharuch viability?
qa_highlights.answer: Wanhua added a 360 kt plant. Indian market is about 120 kt; GNFC capacity is 70,000 tpa. Major foam makers are customers. No plan to shut Bharuch; cost gap to Dahej narrowing with captive power.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 average prices for TDI, aniline, acetic acid and weak nitric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: TDI ~INR 285,000, aniline ~INR 238,000, acetic acid ~INR 72,840 (Q1 INR 62,600), WNA ~INR 28,500 on 100% basis. Management offered to share remaining figures offline.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory build and liquidation in Q1-Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 inventory fell INR 236 crore; cumulative liquidation across Q1 and Q2 was INR 533 crore.

risks_watch: Chemical realisation erosion (WNA, TGU, AN Melt) and the impact of Chinese TDI capacity from Wanhua's 360 kt addition.
Energy cost volatility: coal-linked fuel and steam cost, gas and crude pass-through with lag; management said linkage is currently unreliable.
Wage settlement accruals likely to keep hitting employee cost in coming quarters.
Subsidy receivables rising; Rabi nutrient-based subsidy rates pending and NITI Aayog review of urea fixed costs.
Coal-based plant full-scale test run in Q3 FY27 and TDI/acetic restart stability; one project three months behind schedule.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and guarded: management repeatedly declined to comment on Q3, current prices or spreads, citing price-sensitive rules and uncertainty from the war-driven energy market. Confident on Q2 operating facts and cash position, but evasive on forward margins.
